findings.title: Coin flips are positional and invariant to the canary pool, enabling silent audit invalidation under key reuse
findings.claim: The in/out coin mask is a pure function of (key, num_canaries) — `coin_rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN).seed); in_mask = coin_rng.random(num_canaries) < 0.5` — so it is byte-identical across every candidate_indices value (pinned as intended behavior by tests/auditing/test_audit.py:467 `np.testing.assert_array_equal(pooled._in_mask, expected_mask)`), prefix-stable across num_canaries, and fully caller-computable before the pool is committed. Coins are then assigned to records positionally through the selection permutation of np.unique(pool). This makes the one-run fair-coin independence assumption unverifiable and easy to violate silently whenever a key is reused across pool iterations, which the docs themselves encourage (every snippet uses key(42)).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Inflation/false alarm: a caller (or an automated canary-crafting loop) that computes the deterministic record→coin map before training — I reproduced it in 6 lines from public API — and correlates canary content with the precomputed coin (e.g. places duplicates of always-in rows at coin=in indices and OOD garbage at coin=out indices) gets honest loss_scores that separate perfectly regardless of DP noise. Demonstrated end-to-end: for a mechanism with ZERO leakage (scores set equal to the precomputed coins via public canary_scores), one_run reports eps_delta().epsilon_at(delta=0) = 5.81 and gdp epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 38.2 at m=1000 — the audit 'lower bound' exceeds any real guarantee. (b) Silent corruption on drift: editing the pool by ONE element under the same key reassigns in/out for ~half the shared records (measured 45/100 flipped between candidate_indices=range(1000,1100) and range(1000,1101)). A workflow that recreates the partition in a separate eval script (natural, since coin_flip is documented as 'reproducible' from the key) with a pool that drifted by one record silently splits honest scores against membership labels that are ~uncorrelated with the ones used in training — one_run raises nothing and reports a meaningless epsilon in either direction.
evidence: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/_coin_flip.py:353-358: `rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _CANARY_SELECTION_DOMAIN).seed); canary_indices = rng.choice(population, size=num_canaries, replace=False); coin_rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN).seed); in_mask = np.asarray(coin_rng.random(num_canaries) < _INCLUSION_PROBABILITY, dtype=bool)` — coin stream never sees the pool or the selected identities.

packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_audit.py:440-467: test_coin_flip_uses_reproducible_domain_separated_keys asserts `pooled._in_mask == expected_mask` where pooled uses candidate_indices=range(50,100) and expected_mask comes from the un-pooled call — the invariance is test-pinned.

Empirical (run in this session, commit 4b13d82): mask full==poolA True; mask full==poolB True (pool sizes 100 and 101); records whose in/out flipped after adding one pool element: 45 of 100; caller-side coin prediction from fold_in(key,'opaque.auditing.canary_selection')/'opaque.auditing.coin_flip' matches cf.in_indices exactly; coin stream prefix-stable across num_canaries (mask[:100] of m=200 equals mask of m=100).

Empirical inflation demo: cf2 = coin_flip(ds, num_canaries=1000, key=key(42), candidate_indices=range(1000)); scores = 1.0 where index in cf2.in_indices else 0.0; one_run(canary_scores(...), coin_flip=cf2) → eps_delta epsilon_at(delta=0) = 5.809, gdp epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 38.25 — with scores that contain no information about any training run.

docs/user-guide/auditing.md (Stronger canaries): 'Fix the pool before target training, independently of that run's membership coins' — an obligation the API makes uncheckable (the coins are a deterministic public function of key and num_canaries, computable before the pool is fixed) and does not detect violations of.

One-run validity requires the membership coins to be uniform and independent of the guessing strategy/canary choice: Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski (2023), arXiv:2305.08846, Theorem 5.2 (coins S_i i.i.d. and independent of everything the adversary controls); the same assumption carries into Xiang et al. (2025), arXiv:2509.08704.
findings.fix_sketch: Fold the canonicalized selected canary identities (or a hash of the validated pool) into the coin-flip domain — e.g. fold_in(key, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN, blake2-of-sorted-pool) — so any pool or num_canaries change rerandomizes all coins, invalidating precomputed coin knowledge across pool iterations; additionally record a fingerprint (dataset_size, pool hash) on CoinFlip and provide serialization so eval scripts reload the training-time partition instead of recreating it; document that the audit key must be drawn fresh after the pool is committed and never reused across pool designs.

findings.title: loss_scores/gradient_scores silently score a wrong dataset when canary indices happen to be in range
findings.claim: The verified scoring path (`_IndexedCanaries.__getitem__` → `self._dataset[int(self._canary_indices[position])]`, _helpers.py:79-81) accepts any `dataset` object with no check that it is the dataset the partition was created from — CoinFlip records neither the dataset size nor any fingerprint. The crafted-canary workflow introduced by PR #751 doubles the number of dataset objects in flight (base `dataset` vs concatenated `audited`, plus `train_data` subsets), and passing the wrong one is only caught when some canary index exceeds its length; otherwise every score is silently computed for the wrong record and one_run accepts the result.
findings.failure_scenario: cf = coin_flip(audited, num_canaries=4, key=key(3), candidate_indices=range(0,4)) (pool at the head, e.g. crafted canaries prepended); user scores with dataset=cf.train_subset(audited) instead of audited. Because the out-canary removal shifts Subset positions, canary 2 is scored as record 3 and canary 3 as record 4 — demonstrated: wrong scores [-0.0,-1.0,-9.0,-16.0] vs correct [-0.0,-1.0,-4.0,-9.0], and one_run(...) returned OneRunEstimate(n_in=3, n_out=1, auc=0.667) without any error. The resulting epsilon is silently wrong in either direction. With a tail pool (the documented pattern) the same mistake fails loudly with IndexError, which hides the hazard during doc-following development and surfaces it only when the pool placement changes.
evidence: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_helpers.py:79-81: `def __getitem__(self, position): return position, self._dataset[int(self._canary_indices[position])]` — no relationship to the partition's dataset is verified; _scoring_loader (:137-156) validates batch_size and reference_scores types only.

packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/_coin_flip.py:136-157: CoinFlip stores only num_canaries, canary_indices, _in_mask, in_indices, out_indices — no dataset_size or fingerprint to check against.

Empirical (this session, 4b13d82): head-pool cf over a 20-record dataset scored against its own 19-record train_subset produced shifted, wrong scores that one_run accepted (output quoted in failure_scenario); the same mistake with a tail pool raised IndexError — fail-loud only by accident of index ranges.
The July audit's clean-note (master list, defended-item 12) covered only train_indices set-subtraction, not the scoring path; no OPEN issue tracks this.
findings.fix_sketch: Record dataset_size (and optionally a cheap content fingerprint of a few canary rows) on CoinFlip at creation; have _scoring_loader assert len(dataset) == cf.dataset_size before building the loader, with an error message naming the concatenated-audited-dataset requirement. This turns both the base-dataset and train-subset mistakes into deterministic failures instead of range-dependent silent corruption.

clean_areas: Checked pool validation fails closed by executing coin_flip at 4b13d82 with duplicates, negative indices, out-of-range indices, float dtype, bool dtype, 2-D arrays, sets, and bool/float num_canaries — all raise ValueError/TypeError in _candidate_pool (_coin_flip.py:279-301) or numpy before any partition exists; empty pool with num_canaries=0 builds a 0-canary partition that one_run rejects at _estimate.py:81-82 ('Both in_scores and out_scores must be non-empty'), so a degenerate audit cannot emit an epsilon.

Checked selection RNG by code trace and execution: sampling is uniform without replacement over np.unique(pool) via numpy Generator.choice; pool order irrelevance verified by running ascending vs descending pools (identical canary_indices and mask, matching test_candidate_pool_order_is_irrelevant); selection and coin streams remain domain-separated through distinct string tags 'opaque.auditing.canary_selection' / 'opaque.auditing.coin_flip' hashed via blake2b fold_in (engine/random/_engine.py:27-35,58-112) — the OPQ-128 fix survives intact on the new pooled path.

Checked that the epsilon-lower-bound machinery conditions correctly on the pool by tracing one_run → _best_r_u → _eps_delta/_stats: every statistic uses only realized n_in/n_out and m = n_in + n_out = num_canaries (_estimate.py:92-103,141-161; _eps_delta.py:69-71; _stats.py search_ceiling(m,...)); no code path assumes canaries are a uniform sample of the full dataset (validity per Steinke et al. Thm 5.2 holds for any fixed canary set given fair coins), and unselected pool members correctly remain always-in training rows since train_indices excludes only out_indices (_coin_flip.py:165-178) — matching the user-guide claim verbatim.

Checked score-join integrity for pooled partitions by executing split_scores/_join_scores (_coin_flip.py:194-276) with foreign identifiers, duplicated identifiers, missing identifiers, bare arrays, and a uint64 pool — all mismatches raise (TypeError/ValueError) and uint64 indices join correctly, so pool-based canary identifiers cannot silently misalign scores with coins.

Checked the PR's documentation claims: the newly cited paper Dagréou & Bellet, arXiv:2605.27292 'Detectability in Diversity: Improved Canary Crafting for Privacy Auditing in One Run' exists with exactly that title (fetched the arXiv abstract page through the proxy); the reference-doc raise conditions ('malformed or fewer than num_canaries') match the implementation; README's 'injection'→'partitioning' correction closes OPQ-127's wording defect accurately; the tutorial's 'every random-labelled record' claim matches its torch.randint label construction (privacy_auditing.ipynb line ~95); the docs' 'If the pool is larger, its unselected records remain ordinary always-in training data' and 'Pool order does not affect a seeded partition' claims were verified by execution.

Checked duplicate-canary handling: duplicate pool indices are rejected (_candidate_pool np.unique size check, tested); content-level duplicates (a pool record duplicating a non-canary training row) are undetectable by any index-based API but can only weaken the attack (out-canaries score like members, deflating epsilon-hat while the lower-bound semantics stay valid), and the user guide's interference paragraph covers this failure mode.

Checked all 12 new pool-related tests pass in the current tree (pytest -k 'pool or candidate or negative_num': 12 passed), and confirmed the four example scripts were touched only by an advisory print line — none pass candidate_indices, so no example workflow changed behavior.

Checked that the pre-existing post-hoc threshold selection in _best_r_u (max over thresholds of TP+TN without multiplicity correction) and null-calibration of the one-run tests are NOT worsened by the pool PR (m and the statistic's semantics are unchanged); these concerns are tracked by OPEN issues #327 and #376 and were not re-reported.
